rounds.text: M K Proteins Ltd demonstrates superior asset efficiency, generating a Return on Assets of 5.21% which comfortably outperforms the sector benchmark of 3.52% [E8]. This operational profitability is further supported by a remarkable historical track record, evidenced by a 10-year median Return on Equity of 18% and a 5-year median Return on Equity of 17% [E25, E26]. Trading at a modest share price of ₹ 4.19 with a market capitalisation of ₹ 157 Cr, the company maintains a sensible book value of ₹ 2.03 and a price-to-book ratio of 2.06x [E2, E3]. Conceded: [E43, E44, E45, E68, E70].

M K Proteins Ltd carries significant valuation and fundamental risks, driven by a rich pricing structure that outpaces both sector benchmarks and underlying performance [E70]. The stock trades at a P/E of 23.22x against a sector benchmark of 19.15x, alongside a price-to-book ratio of 2.06x that also exceeds its sector benchmark [E6, E7]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis puts intrinsic value at Rs 2 per share compared to the market price of Rs 4.19, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -103.9% [E43, E44]. Fundamental momentum is clearly deteriorating, as evidenced by a 5-year trend where price grew 36% while profit dropped -8%, showing the stock has run far ahead of fundamentals [E54]. This weakness is underscored by a declining return on equity trajectory, falling from a 10-year median of 18% and a 5-year median of 17% down to a 3-year median of 13% and a recent 9% [E25, E26, E27, E28]. Conceded: the company demonstrates a 10-year median return on equity of 18% and a 5-year median of 17% [E25, E26].

While the bear points to a higher P/E of 23.22x against the sector benchmark of 19.15x [E6], this premium multiple is justified by superior asset utilization, evidenced by an ROA of 5.21% that outpaces the sector benchmark of 3.52% [E8]. Conceded: a discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 2 per share, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -103.9% [E43, E44], yet backward-looking cash flow models routinely miss structural earning power demonstrated across broader operating cycles. The bear's critique of deteriorating ROE ignores the company's proven long-term compound capability, specifically a robust 10-year median return on equity of 18% and a 5-year median of 17% [E25, E26]. Furthermore, citing the price-to-book ratio of 2.06x against the sector benchmark of 1.79x [E7] simply reflects market recognition of this higher structural capital efficiency rather than an unearned valuation premium.

Conceded: the company demonstrates a 10-year median ROE of 18% and a 5-year median of 17% [E25, E26], alongside an ROA of 5.21% beating the sector benchmark of 3.52% [E8]. However, those historical metrics completely mask a sharp structural collapse in profitability, evidenced by the 3-year median ROE dropping to 13% [E27] and the last year's ROE plunging all the way down to 9% [E28], or 8.95% against the sector's 8.45% [E9]. That backward-looking median defence also ignores the fundamental reality that today's price is trading at a premium P/E of 23.22x versus the sector benchmark of 19.15x [E6], while a discounted cash flow explicitly values the business at just Rs 2 per share against a market price of Rs 4.19 [E43]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF reveals that the current market price already bakes in an unwarranted 9.8% earnings growth expectation when the base case assumes 0.0% [E45]. Finally, the 5-year trend confirms that price has grown 36% while profit fell 8%, proving the stock has severely outrun its deteriorating fundamentals [E54].
